title: Bakery-Style Cinnamon Buns
description: Soft, pillowy, buttery, and swirled with cinnamon sugar — just like your favourite bakery.

method.instruction: In a large bowl, combine 250 ml of warm milk, yeast, and sugar. Let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Add flour, 7 g of the salt, 75 g of melted unsalted butter, and egg. Mix until a smooth, slightly sticky dough forms. Knead for 8–10 minutes until elastic.
Cover and let dough rise in a warm place until doubled, about 1–1½ hours.
Roll dough into a rectangle approximately 30 cm × 40 cm. Brush evenly with the remaining 75 g of melted unsalted butter, then sprinkle with brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll the dough tightly into a log starting from the long edge. Pinch the seam to seal. Cut into 10 even slices.
Place buns in a greased tin with space between each. Cover and let rise for 30–45 minutes until puffy.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Bake buns for 20–25 minutes until golden brown.
Whisk together icing sugar, the remaining 30 ml of milk, vanilla extract, and the remaining 1 g of salt until smooth. Drizzle over warm buns.

notes.title: Warm Milk
notes.content: Milk should be warm to the touch, not hot — approximately 40°C. Too hot and it will kill the yeast. If you can comfortably hold your finger in it, it is the right temperature.

notes.title: Clean Cuts
notes.content: Use unflavoured dental floss to cut the dough log — slide it under, cross the ends, and pull. It gives clean cuts without squashing the spirals.

notes.title: Serving Tip
notes.content: Best eaten warm on the day they are baked. Reheat leftover buns in the microwave for 20–30 seconds to soften the glaze.
